Preflight Demo Program
DOC-0003 2026-10-14
A Follow-Up Cadence for Blocked Issues
POLICY
Effective date: 2026-10-14
Custodian: PERSON-0018, TEAM-0006
Scope: Coordination follow-up for items selected from the blocked-issue
queue.
~ The owning-team lead reviews the dependency slip at 10:15 and again at 15:15
each working day. Record the answer needed, the team being contacted, and
the next promised contact time. These checkpoints organize follow-up; they
do not describe the condition of an aircraft.
— At the morning checkpoint, ask whether the dependency has a named
contact and a useful next action. At the afternoon checkpoint, carry any
unanswered request into the next shift's list with the same owning team.
Preserve a missed contact as a dated entry instead of erasing it when a new
appointment is made.
— Use question-first escalation if the contact cannot be arranged. Begin with
the answer needed, then identify the role responsible for seeking it and the
next contact time. Send that request to the duty chair. A general instruction
to hurry gives the chair no decision to make.
~ Keep scheduling escalation separate from a priority-change request. A
delayed answer requires a follow-up plan; any proposed priority change
needs its own written justification and review.
_ For the controls desk example, file the dependency slip under
DEMO-AIR-0001 and ISSUE-0077. TASK-0203 may identify the associated
discussion without implying any recorded category.
Revision note: This edition introduces the afternoon carry-forward check and
preserves missed-contact history.
D. Worker 0018
Demo Worker 0018, Demo Team 06
